description: Precalculus, geometry and linear algebra with the computer in hand: functions, limits, vectors and matrices computed and plotted in R and MATLAB as they are learned. Taught to the depth of a first-year linear algebra and precalculus sequence for engineers.
modelledOn: Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications
outcomes: Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions and use them in integration and transforms.
Evaluate limits and test continuity algebraically and numerically.
Model growth, decay and scaling with exponential and logarithmic functions and solve the resulting equations.
Solve problems in coordinate geometry and trigonometry that arise in graphics and navigation.
Compute with vectors and matrices: dot and cross products, systems of equations, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues.
Use R and MATLAB to compute, plot and check every technique in the course.

units.title: Algebra review and partial fractions
topics: Polynomials, factoring, polynomial division, the remainder and factor theorems
Rational expressions and proper versus improper fractions
Partial fractions: distinct linear, repeated linear and irreducible quadratic factors
Applications: summing series, inverse Laplace transforms preview, integrating rational functions
Getting started with R and MATLAB: variables, vectors, plotting

units.title: Functions, limits and continuity
topics: Functions, domain and range, composition and inverses; graphs of standard functions
Limits from tables and graphs; limit laws; limits at infinity and asymptotes
Continuity and the intermediate value theorem; piecewise functions
Numerical estimation of limits in software; floating-point pitfalls
Sequences and convergence

units.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
topics: Exponential growth and decay; the number e; compound interest and mobile-money savings
Logarithms, change of base, laws of logarithms; solving exponential and logarithmic equations
Log scales: decibels, pH, Richter, and plotting algorithm running times
Why log n appears in computer science: binary search, tree height, bits needed

units.title: Geometry and trigonometry
topics: Coordinate geometry: distance, midpoint, lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses
Trigonometric functions, the unit circle, identities, inverse trigonometric functions
Solving triangles: sine and cosine rules; bearings and surveying problems
Polar coordinates and parametric curves
Geometry for graphics: angles between lines, reflection, rotation, areas of polygons

units.title: Vectors
topics: Vectors in 2D and 3D: magnitude, direction, unit vectors, components
Addition, scalar multiplication, linear combinations, span and linear independence
Dot product, angle between vectors, projections; cross product and areas
Lines and planes in space; distance from a point to a plane
Applications: forces, velocities, computer graphics, cosine similarity of documents

units.title: Matrices and systems of linear equations
topics: Matrix notation, addition, multiplication, transpose; special matrices
Systems of linear equations; Gaussian and Gauss-Jordan elimination; row echelon form; rank
Determinants: cofactor expansion, properties, Cramer's rule
Inverse of a matrix; solving AX = B; LU decomposition preview
Matrices as transformations: rotation, scaling, shear; composition of transformations
Markov chains and PageRank as matrix problems

units.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
topics: Characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices
Diagonalisation and powers of a matrix
Applications: population models, vibration, principal component analysis preview
Numerical computation of eigenvalues in R and MATLAB

units.title: Applications in R and MATLAB
topics: Matrix operations, solving systems, determinants, inverses and eigen-decomposition in both tools
Plotting functions, curves, vectors and transformations
Fitting a line to data by least squares as a matrix problem
A capstone: image transformation or a simple recommendation using vector similarity
